The system comprises a B0 magnet configured to generate a B0 magnetic field for an imaging region of the system; a noise reduction system configured to detect and suppress at least some electromagnetic noise in the operating environment of the system; and electromagnetic shielding configured to attenuate at least some of the electromagnetic noise in the operating environment, the electromagnetic shielding being arranged to shield a portion of the imaging region. outputs.L2:
In certain implementations, a portable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) system includes a B0 magnet designed to generate a B0 magnetic field within the system’s imaging region. The system also includes a noise-mitigation system that detects and reduces at least a portion of the electromagnetic interference present in the portable MRI system’s operating environment. Electromagnetic shielding is further included to diminish some of that environmental electromagnetic interference, with the shielding positioned to cover part of the imaging region.

In some implementations, the electromagnetic shielding includes one or more shield structures adjustably attached to the housing, allowing the level of electromagnetic shielding provided to the imaging region to be changed. In other implementations, the imaging region of the portable MRI system is substantially unshielded.
outputs.L3:
A portable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) system includes a B0 magnet configured to generate a B0 magnetic field within an imaging region. The system further includes a noise-reduction system that detects electromagnetic noise in the surrounding operating environment and suppresses its effects on acquired MRI signals.

The portable MRI system may also include electromagnetic shielding configured to attenuate environmental electromagnetic noise. Unlike conventional shielding arrangements that enclose the entire imaging region, the shielding may cover or surround only a fraction of the imaging region. In certain implementations, at least one electromagnetic shield structure is adjustably coupled to the system housing, allowing the position or extent of the shield to be changed and, consequently, the amount of electromagnetic shielding to be varied. In other configurations, the imaging region may be operated with substantially no electromagnetic shielding, with environmental noise addressed primarily by the noise-reduction system.
outputs.L4:
A portable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) system includes a main B0 magnet configured to generate the static magnetic field required for imaging. Because portable systems may be operated outside conventional, permanently shielded MRI suites, the system also incorporates active electromagnetic-noise detection and suppression. One or more sensors monitor radio-frequency or other electromagnetic interference in and around the imaging region, and a suppression system uses the detected signals to reduce artifacts and preserve image quality.

The MRI system further includes adjustable electromagnetic shielding that can be positioned according to the needs of a particular examination or operating environment. The shielding may cover only part of the imaging region, substantially enclose the entire region, or be retracted so that the region remains unshielded. Partial shielding can provide targeted attenuation while maintaining patient access, visibility, ventilation, and ease of use. Full shielding may be selected in environments with high interference, whereas little or no shielding may be appropriate in quieter locations or when maximum accessibility is required.

By combining active noise suppression with selectively configurable shielding, the system can adapt to changing electromagnetic conditions without relying on a fixed, room-sized shielded enclosure. This variable-shielding approach provides effective noise attenuation and supports reliable MRI operation while preserving the portability, flexibility, and rapid deployment advantages of the system across hospitals, clinics, emergency settings, and other locations.
outputs.L5:
## Understanding the Word “According”

“According” is commonly used to show that information comes from a particular person, document, or source. It usually appears in the phrase **“according to.”** For example, “According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow” means that the forecast is the source of this information.

The phrase can also describe something that follows a rule, plan, or expectation. In the sentence “Everything went according to plan,” it means events happened as intended. Similarly, “Employees are paid according to their experience” indicates that experience determines their pay.

When using “according to,” it is important to identify the source clearly and accurately. The phrase is useful in academic writing, journalism, reports, and everyday conversation because it helps distinguish verified information or another person’s opinion from the writer’s own views.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing a portable MRI system with a B0 magnet, active electromagnetic noise detection and suppression, and partial, adjustable, or optional shielding around the imaging region.
counterfactuals.output: A portable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) system includes a main magnet configured to generate a static B0 magnetic field within an imaging region, a gradient subsystem, and a radiofrequency transmit-and-receive subsystem. One or more electromagnetic sensors are positioned in, adjacent to, or remote from the imaging region and are configured to detect ambient electromagnetic interference. A controller processes signals from the electromagnetic sensors to estimate interference affecting acquired magnetic resonance data and suppresses the interference by adaptive filtering, reference-noise cancellation, feedforward cancellation, feedback cancellation, modification of an acquisition sequence, or combinations thereof. The system further includes an electromagnetic shield disposed at least partially around the imaging region. The shield may be removable, collapsible, repositionable, selectively deployable, or adjustable in geometry, coverage, attenuation, or electrical characteristics, and may define one or more openings for patient access, ventilation, viewing, or equipment passage. In some configurations, the shield is omitted and electromagnetic noise suppression is performed primarily by the sensors and controller. The combined shielding and active noise-suppression arrangements facilitate magnetic resonance imaging in non-shielded or variably shielded environments while maintaining portability and access to a subject.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical summary of an invention for portable magnetic resonance imaging that can operate in electromagnetically noisy environments without requiring a fully shielded room.
counterfactuals.output: A portable MRI system enables imaging in electromagnetically noisy environments without a fully shielded room. The system combines a compact, low-field magnet and localized RF shielding with one or more external electromagnetic interference reference sensors. During signal acquisition, the sensors measure ambient noise independently of the patient’s MR signal. Adaptive filtering or model-based reconstruction uses these reference measurements to estimate and remove interference from the receive-coil data. Optional synchronized RF transmission, frequency tracking, and interference-aware pulse sequences further improve robustness. The integrated design reduces installation requirements while preserving diagnostically useful image quality in settings such as emergency departments, intensive care units, ambulances, and remote clinics.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, using formal patent language beginning with “According to some aspects,” a portable MRI apparatus featuring variable electromagnetic shielding coupled to its housing.
counterfactuals.output: According to some aspects, a portable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) apparatus comprises a housing configured for transport between imaging locations, a magnet assembly disposed within the housing and configured to generate a magnetic field within an imaging region, one or more gradient coils, and a radio-frequency transmit/receive assembly. A variable electromagnetic shielding assembly is coupled to the housing and is selectively configurable between a transport configuration and one or more deployed configurations. The shielding assembly may include telescoping, foldable, inflatable, rollable, or otherwise movable shielding members comprising electrically conductive and/or magnetically permeable materials. In a deployed configuration, the shielding members at least partially surround the imaging region to attenuate external electromagnetic interference and/or limit emission of radio-frequency energy from the apparatus. An actuator or user-operable mechanism may vary a position, geometry, overlap, grounding state, or attenuation characteristic of the shielding assembly. A controller may adjust the shielding assembly based on a detected interference level, an imaging protocol, or a measured shielding effectiveness, thereby enabling operation of the portable MRI apparatus in environments having differing electromagnetic conditions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent disclosure paragraph covering three embodiments of portable MRI shielding: partial shielding of the imaging region, an adjustable shield structure, and substantially no shielding, together with active noise reduction.
counterfactuals.output: In various embodiments, a portable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) system includes an active noise-reduction subsystem and may employ different levels of passive electromagnetic shielding. In a first embodiment, a shield is positioned to at least partially surround an imaging region, while leaving one or more portions open to facilitate patient access, portability, ventilation, or clinician access. In a second embodiment, the shield includes an adjustable structure comprising one or more movable, foldable, telescoping, removable, inflatable, or reconfigurable shielding elements, thereby permitting the extent, position, or geometry of shielding to be adapted to a patient, anatomy, operating environment, or imaging protocol. In a third embodiment, the MRI system operates with substantially no passive shielding around the imaging region. In each embodiment, the active noise-reduction subsystem may include one or more reference sensors configured to detect ambient electromagnetic interference, processing circuitry configured to estimate an interference component present in acquired magnetic-resonance signals, and a controller configured to reduce the interference by adaptive filtering, cancellation-signal generation, acquisition-sequence adjustment, post-processing, or any combination thereof, thereby enabling diagnostically useful imaging in environments having variable electromagnetic noise.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: What might the abstract of a patent claim for a portable low-field MRI system look like if it combines a B0 magnet, environmental electromagnetic-noise suppression, and shielding whose coverage can be varied?
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

A portable low-field magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) system includes a B0 magnet configured to generate a main magnetic field within an imaging region, a radiofrequency subsystem configured to excite and detect magnetic resonance signals, and an electromagnetic-noise suppression subsystem configured to reduce environmental interference detected during image acquisition. The noise suppression subsystem may include one or more reference sensors and a controller that adaptively removes correlated interference from received magnetic resonance signals. The system further includes an electromagnetic shield having an adjustable configuration that provides selectively variable coverage around at least a portion of the imaging region, a subject, or the radiofrequency subsystem. The shield may be extended, retracted, repositioned, or assembled in sections to accommodate different anatomical regions and operating environments. By combining low-field operation, adaptive environmental-noise suppression, and variable-coverage shielding, the system enables portable MRI acquisition in locations lacking a fixed radiofrequency-shielded room.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
